### Historical audit — S0108

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r2/scene_rsi_pilot/C2/selection/commons_138420790/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to JSONL lines in this file. No observations were split across chunks.

| Evidence | Observed operations and limits |
|---|---|
| Goal — line 1 | The student was asked to reconstruct a single indoor photograph as an editable SceneAct/Blender scene, matching viewpoint, objects and materials. The student’s interpretation was an industrial kitchen; the reference image itself is not visible to this audit. |
| Initial build — lines 3–5 | Code created multiple semantic assets: island, cabinets, two ovens, kettle, hood and two posts, plus room geometry. It specified colors, a procedural wood material, a camera and three lights. Island fittings and plinth were grouped with the island; grouping is not proof of physical contact or completeness. Execution reported success and saved a render and blend file. |
| Camera exploration — lines 7, 9–12 | After receiving the first render, the student estimated a foreground wall obscured the scene and hypothesized that the camera was outside the left wall. It changed camera position, target and lens; step 2 executed successfully. The diagnosis and visual improvement are not independently verified here. |
| Geometry exploration — lines 13, 15–18 | After receiving step 2, the student estimated incorrect island proportions and low hood and worktop. Step 3 narrowed and deepened the island, raised its counter and hood, scaled rear cabinetry, moved the kettle and foreground post, and derived island parts from shared dimensions. It retained the camera and lighting. Step 3 executed successfully. These coordinated edits do not isolate which change helped. |
| Final review — lines 19–22 | The student received step 3’s render, responded `DONE`, and step 3 was selected. All three executions reported `ok: true`; that is build/render success, not independent confirmation of reconstruction accuracy. |

**Teacher input and autonomy:** No separate teacher intervention, diagnosis, proposed patch, or adoption is recorded. The initial shared procedure and subsequent runner prompts supplied general instructions and render feedback, which the student demonstrably received; the specific camera and geometry hypotheses and revisions were the student’s. No external tool exploration is recorded in the student sessions (lines 2, 8, 14, 20).

**Outcome and uncertainty:** A non-empty scene was built and the latest successful step selected; formal visual correctness remains **unknown**. The images are referenced, not available to this audit. Thus object counts and semantic labels are code/student claims, not verified reference content. The code provides a procedural texture but does not establish that it was applied to the intended rendered meshes; its name-based selection depends on realized names. Pose here means object placement and orientation, not an observed human pose. Actual supports, sink depth, occlusion, camera framing, lighting quality and hood/ceiling clearance remain unverified; notably, the raised hood’s specified top exceeds the ceiling deck height. No independent visual or geometric test resolves those issues (lines 15–17).

**Transferable lesson:** Separate render success from scene fidelity, and track dependent fittings when resizing assemblies. **Task-specific hypothesis:** the wall obstruction and island proportions motivated these particular changes, but their causal accuracy and the final match remain unresolved.
